current.charge: Searched ~83,000 Flock cameras nationwide to track a woman who had an abortion.
current.roast:
For running a nationwide dragnet across roughly 83,000 Flock cameras to hunt down a woman — not a fugitive, not a violent suspect — but a woman who had an abortion.

The search got logged as a "missing person / welfare check." Court records tell a different story: investigators were reportedly eyeing criminal charges. She'd harmed no one. She was the target anyway — tracked across cameras in states where she hadn't broken a single law.

This is Flock in one sentence: a system sold as "public safety," turned into a personal manhunt machine, pointed at an innocent person. Congrats, Johnson County — you played yourself, and you handed the rest of us the clearest reason yet to tear this network down.
